title: Pacer synthesis latency-cost notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick exploratory notes from the Pacer synthesis runs. Goal: validate a lightweight admission/pacing layer ("pacer") that smooths short-duration spikes to reduce tail latency with limited extra GPU cost. This doc records the harness, raw results (text charts), qualitative observations, and open questions for follow-up experiments.

Test harness and knobs
---------------------
- Model: small-medium decoder-only open model (approx 8B eq) quantized fp16/INT8 mix; same model binary for all runs.
- Hardware: 4x A100-sim nodes (logical partition used in benches), each node treated as independent GPU pool.
- Traffic profiles:
  1) steady_100: 100 sustained QPS for 30m (baseline throughput target)
  2) microburst: baseline 150 QPS with 12x spikes to 1800 QPS lasting 6s every 3min (total 20 spikes)
  3) sessionized: 1k concurrent sessions, geometric turn length (mean 6 turns), arrival poisson -> mimics chat app
- Pacer knobs: smoothing_factor s ∈ {0.0, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8} (0.0 == no pacer), slot_multiplier (1.0/1.3), max_hold_ms 120
- Measurement: token-latency (ms) per response, p50/p95/p99, GPU tokens/s, request admission latency (enqueue->start), cost model: $0.60 per GPU-hour equivalent used (internal unit).

Compact results (selected)
-------------------------
Note: these are median-of-3 run aggregates; numbers rounded. Costs are amortized to a per-10k-requests bucket for quick comparison.

Profile: microburst (spike-focused)
----------------------------------
Baseline (s=0.0):
- median: 85 ms | p95: 320 ms | p99: 420 ms | tokens/sec/GPU: 950 | cost/10k req: $1.12
Pacer s=0.6, slot_mult=1.0:
- median: 92 ms | p95: 180 ms | p99: 220 ms | tokens/sec/GPU: 920 | cost/10k req: $1.16
Delta (approx): p99 -48%, cost +3.6%

Profile: steady_100
------------------
Baseline (s=0.0):
- median: 72 ms | p95: 105 ms | p99: 140 ms | tokens/sec/GPU: 980 | cost/10k req: $0.95
Pacer s=0.6:
- median: 75 ms | p95: 108 ms | p99: 145 ms | tokens/sec/GPU: 975 | cost/10k req: $0.97
Delta: negligible latency change, cost +2.1%

Profile: sessionized
--------------------
Baseline: p99 380 ms, admission jitter high (spiky tail when sessions multiplex)
Pacer s=0.6: p99 210 ms, admission jitter reduced, tokens/sec/GPU -3.5%

ASCII charts (microburst p99 over time - illustrative)
-----------------------------------------------------
Time (s) around spike:   -30   -20   -10    0    10    20    30
Baseline p99 (ms):       120   150   320  420   350   180   130
Pacer s=0.6 p99 (ms):    90   110   160  220   170   120    95

Bar-style comparison (microburst p99)
-----------------------------------
Baseline p99:  [#########################] 420 ms
Pacer s=0.6:  [###############         ] 220 ms
(visual approximate; each # ~16 ms)

Observations
------------
- Pacer strongly reduces p99 during short spikes with modest throughput loss and small cost increase. The effect is most pronounced for short (<= 10s) high-amplitude spikes.
- For steady loads the pacer has minimal downside; small added queuing increases median by a few ms but p95/p99 unaffected.
- Sessionized workloads benefit because pacer reduces admission jitter that arises from session affinity and KV-cache warmups.
- Cost delta is primarily from slightly lower GPU-util efficiency (fewer tight packing opportunities) + marginally longer average request lifetime.

Tradeoffs & heuristics
---------------------
- Smoothing_factor sweet spot: 0.5–0.7 gives good p99 reduction with <=4% cost delta in our runs. Above 0.8 you start to see queuing add to median latency for medium-duration surges.
- slot_multiplier 1.3 helps keep short bursts absorbed without triggering preemptive scaling; combine with max_hold_ms=100–150ms.
- Prefer pacer in hosted-tier offering for tiers that buy p99 SLOs; give as an opt-in knob with cost-impact warning.

Open questions / next experiments
-------------------------------
- Longer burst lengths (15–30s) — does pacer just defer cost to autoscaling or still reduce tail? Need run with autoscale enabled.
- Interaction with KV cache prefetch: does pacer increase cold-eviction probability? Add per-request KV hit metric.
- Multi-tenant interaction: test with adversarial tenant spikiness to validate isolation.
- Evaluate under different model sizes / seq-length distributions (long-context chats).

Quick notes to product/console teams
-----------------------------------
- Consider adding a "burst-smoothing" flag in console with an estimated cost delta calculator (show per-100k requests).
- UX: show expected p99 improvement band (low/median/high) and sample ASCII timeline in the knob tooltip.

References & links
------------------
- PR: github:repo/pr/1223 (pacer prototype)
- Jira: PLAT-4521 (pacer integration epic)
- Confluence: PLAT/pacer-synthesis (longer writeup and full-run CSVs)

Next steps (owner: Asha)
-----------------------
- Run lengthened burst experiments (15m config) and add autoscale on/off toggle — target by 2028-12-09.
- Hook KV-hit telemetry into bench harness — target 2028-12-05 (Trevor).
- Draft short one-pager for Hosted-API product inclusion proposing opt-in "burst smoothing" with cost estimator (Marcus).

Questions for the team
----------------------
- Acceptable cost bump for Hosted p99 guarantee? (product to weigh in)
- Should we default pacer on for enterprise Dedicated instances where customers prefer predictable p99 vs minimal cost?
